title: Experimental study of TPU and SEBS additively manufactured leaflets for novel aortic valve polymer TAVI prosthesis.
authors: Alex G Kuchumov; Denis Khoroshev; Aleksandra Kutuzova; Aleksei Baranov; Oleg Krestyaninov; Ekaterina Barbashina; Pavel Zelenchuk; Edward Matjeka; Thanyani Pandelani; Fulufhelo Nemavhola
abstract:
Transcatheter valve implantation is a cutting-edge technology for high and low risk patients with aortic stenosis. Bioprosthetic valves are limited due to several disadvantages as a long-term durability and structural valve degeneration. Polymeric aortic valve leaflet devices represent state-of-the-art technology to overcome limitations of bioprostheses. Nevertheless, more recent biocompatible and biostable polymers have revealed a significant potential. Additionally, 3D additive manufacturing opens new paths for patient-specific design of biomedical implants. Flexible polymers may not only mimic native aortic valve, but also may improve long-term durability. Polyurethanes and styrene polymers are promising materials for modern polymer valves. Nevertheless, mechanical properties of additive manufactured TPU or SEBS leaflets are not properly studied.
Experimental study of TPU and SEBS samples and aortic valve leaflets for novel aortic valve polymer TAVI prosthesis is presented. Tensile tests and compression tests of three types of FDM-printed samples with various filament alignments (axial alignment, transversal alignment, diagonal alignment) were performed. The results of tests confirmed that longitudinal axial alignment achieve a maximum stress compared to transversal and diagonal directions. Compressive tests of TPU and SEBS 3D-manufactured aortic valve leaflets with digital image correlation technology were performed. Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio were evaluated. Moreover, parameters of constitutive models were found.
The TPU tensile specimen exhibits the highest stress/strain values at a speed of 100 mm/min, regardless of the filament alignment pattern. Slightly lower results are observed at a speed of 50 mm/min, which is likely associated with a wide range of plastic deformation. In the case of SEBS, a different pattern is observed: at 500 mm/min, it demonstrates high resistance to fracture, unlike TPU. A comparison of TPU and SEBS specimens at the same speeds and with the same alignment, based on maximum stress values, shows a minimal difference of 4% with the axial alignment at a speed of 50 mm/min; however, when comparing strains, the difference increases to 90%. The results of the compression experiment on aortic valve specimens made of TPU and SEBS at a speed of 30 mm/min showed that TPU force values for is considerably lower (4% of the maximum case), while for SEBS the spread increases to 20% of the maximum case.
SEBS aortic valve leaflets were shown to be stiffer than TPU. It can be a step for choice of stiffer/softer leaflets for patient-specific device. The proposed approach can help manufacturers in elaboration and manufacturing of new TAVI polymer devices design made of TPU and SEBS polymers for clinical applications.

title: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Jin Ha Park; Hyun-Soo Zhang; Suji Lee; Sarah Soh; Young Joo Suh
abstract:
This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR.
A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR.
Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia.
Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

title: New ESC/EACTS guidelines for the management of aortic valve disease: key takeaways and implications of long-term TAVR results based on recent explant and redo-TAVR registry outcomes.
authors: Saptarshi Paul
abstract:
The 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines for valvular heart disease represent a pivotal update, emphasizing earlier intervention for aortic stenosis (AS) and broader indications for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). These changes are driven by randomized trial data demonstrating TAVR's safety in lower-risk patients. However, as TAVR expands to younger cohorts, long-term durability remains a concern.
This narrative review examines key guideline updates for aortic valve disease, focusing on aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), and integrates insights from recent registries (2020-2025) on TAVR explantation and redo-TAVR outcomes. Data from the EXPLANT-TAVR, EXPLANTORREDO-TAVR and FRANCE 2/FRANCE TAVI registries reveal reintervention rates of 0.3-1.7% at 8 years, with redo-TAVR offering superior short-term survival (30-day mortality 1.5-6.2%) compared to explantation (11.9-13.6%). Structural valve deterioration (SVD), leaflet thrombosis, and endocarditis predominate failure causes, underscoring the need for lifetime management strategies.
Implications include refined patient selection, enhanced imaging surveillance, and Heart Team-driven decisions to balance procedural benefits against reintervention risks.

title: Early recognition of PRKAG2 syndrome in an adolescent with a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype and ventricular pre-excitation: a case report.
authors: Zonghui Hou; Xuechen Liu; Mengqi Zhao; Junxiang Pan; Feiyang Wang; Chunbo Wang; Lianyi Wang
abstract:
PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare glycogen-storage cardiomyopathy that can mimic sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). The diagnostic clue is not left ventricular hypertrophy alone, but the combination of hypertrophy with ventricular pre-excitation and conduction-system abnormalities. This pattern is clinically important because PRKAG2 syndrome differs from sarcomeric HCM in disease progression, arrhythmic risk, and long-term management.
A 12-year-old boy presented with recurrent exertional chest tightness. Twelve-lead electrocardiography showed ventricular pre-excitation, and echocardiography demonstrated asymmetric non-obstructive left ventricular hypertrophy. An external Holter report recorded sinus bradycardia and nocturnal pauses. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous PRKAG2 variant, NM_016203:c.1423A>G (p.Lys475Glu), classified as likely pathogenic. The available report from a clinically indicated invasive electrophysiological procedure documented persistent pre-excitation and localized the earliest antegrade ventricular activation to the right midseptal para-Hisian region. Catheter ablation was deferred because no tachyarrhythmia had been documented and ablation near the His bundle carried a substantial risk of atrioventricular block. During approximately 2 years of follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable, with persistent hypertrophy and no major arrhythmic or conduction events.
In adolescents with otherwise unexplained ventricular hypertrophy, ventricular pre-excitation should prompt consideration of PRKAG2 syndrome and other HCM phenocopies, even without a positive family history. Recognition of this combined structural and electrical phenotype may facilitate earlier genetic diagnosis and guide long-term rhythm surveillance. The mechanism of pre-excitation should be described only to the extent supported by the available electrocardiographic and procedural documentation.

title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
authors: Eduardo Keller Saadi; Rodrigo Petersen Saadi; Ana Paula Tagliari
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.
authors: Xianbao Liu; Yuchao Guo; Guangyuan Song; Tongfeng Chen; Guipeng An; Lihan Wang; Yansong Guo; Hao Zhou; Lei Jiang; Xiaomin Chen; Biao Cheng; Guannan Niu; Kai Xu; Yibing Shao; Zhikui Chen; Yining Yang; Zhenfei Fang; Jinjun Liu; Jiancheng Xiu; Jianying Chen; Yongping Bai; Xiaodong Zhuang; Zhenfeng Cheng; Lei Wang; Jizhe Xu; Xiangwen Liang; Ke Han; Haochang Hu; Qiong Liu; Martin B Leon; Jian'an Wang
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
abstract:
Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial.
This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications.
The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications.
A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%).
A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
authors: Ren Wei; Hongpeng Zhang; Minhong Zhang; Cunzhe Fan; Jiang Xiong; Xin Jia; Wei Guo
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: Case Report: Refractory childhood-onset takayasu arteritis with digital clubbing and extensive supra-aortic and lower-limb arterial disease.
authors: Fawzy M Abunejma; Leen M Jabari; Marah Nouredeen Hamad; Tamer O Tamimi; Omair Bseiso; Hisham Aziz Dweik; Raed M A Isayed; Hanan Qunibi; Waleed Alzaro; Wasef Alhroub
abstract: Childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis is rare, and its early picture is often too vague to point at a large-vessel vasculitis. We report a 12-year-old girl who presented with 13 days of recurrent severe retrosternal chest pain and diffuse colicky abdominal pain, on a background of six months of exertional fatigue and painful swelling of the right fingertips, without fever, weight loss or night sweats. Examination showed bilateral digital clubbing, a right arm blood pressure below the 5th percentile with left arm and lower limb readings between the 50th and 90th percentiles, an absent right radial pulse, and weak brachial and right posterior tibial pulses. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 110 mm/h and C-reactive protein 82 to 93 mg/L. Computed tomography angiography showed mild concentric mural thickening of the aortic arch with severe stenosis of the right common and internal carotid arteries, near-occlusion of the right subclavian artery, moderate to severe brachiocephalic stenosis, moderate narrowing of the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries, and moderate stenosis of the right common and superficial femoral arteries. The abdominal aorta and its visceral branches were spared. She met the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES (Ankara 2008) classification criteria for childhood Takayasu arteritis, and the arterial distribution corresponds to Numano type IIa, together with peripheral lower-limb involvement that the Numano scheme does not cover. Disease progressed on intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, methotrexate, aspirin and low-molecular-weight heparin, culminating in an 80% stenosis of the right common femoral artery. Adalimumab was started and later replaced by tocilizumab, after which the femoral peri-arterial inflammatory changes resolved on imaging and acute-phase reactants normalized. Blood pressure asymmetry, pulse deficits and the established stenoses persisted. This case suggests that normal inflammatory markers in childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis can coexist with fixed arterial damage, and that judgements about disease activity are better based on clinical findings and serial imaging together than on acute-phase reactants alone.

title: Sex differences in clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a real-world cohort.
authors: Miriam Estévez Táboas; Julio Echarte-Morales; Ernesto José Ruiz Golcher; Carlos Eduardo Sotomayor-Casillas; André González García; David Neuhalfen; Carla Iglesias-Otero; Elena García-Campos Losada; Nazaret Vázquez-Vázquez; David González Fernández; Hugo Prado Prado; Carmen Cuiñas Fariña; Andrés Antelo-Abeijón; Pablo Juan-Salvadores; Rodrigo Estevez-Loureiro; Jose A Baz Alonso; Andres Iñiguez-Romo; Victor Alfonso Jímenez-Díaz
abstract:
Severe aortic stenosis is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases in the ageing population, and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an effective and less invasive therapeutic alternative. Anatomical, pathophysiological, and clinical differences between women and men may influence outcomes following the procedure. This study aimed to evaluate the association between sex and mortality and procedure-related complications after TAVI in a real-world cohort from the Vigo Health Area.
We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including 1,065 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent transfemoral TAVI between 2010 and 2023. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included bleeding, vascular complications, and new permanent pacemaker implantation. Time-to-event analyses were censored at 365 days; multivariable models used complete-case analysis.
Women were older and had greater frailty and higher surgical risk scores than men. In-hospital and 1-year mortality were similar between sexes. Date-based 30-day mortality was 2.4% in men and 3.7% in women (p = 0.225), and female sex was not independently associated with 30-day mortality after adjustment for age and STS score (adjusted OR 1.79, 95% CI 0.80-3.98; p = 0.154). Female sex was not independently associated with 1-year mortality (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.69-1.66; p = 0.772). Women had more bleeding in unadjusted analyses, but female sex was not significantly associated with any bleeding after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.61, 95% CI 0.92-2.81; p = 0.093). Male sex remained associated with higher odds of new permanent pacemaker implantation (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.03-2.17; p = 0.036).
Sex was not independently associated with short- or 1-year mortality after TAVI. Women had a higher unadjusted incidence of bleeding, whereas men had a higher incidence of new permanent pacemaker implantation that persisted after adjustment. These findings describe sex-related differences in procedural risk profiles but should be interpreted in the context of the observational design and the long study period.

title: Impact of preprocedural frailty on long-term mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Yang Zhan; Yue Mao; Xiaolan Tang; Rong Li; Mei Li; Daoxin Hua
abstract:
This study aimed to investigate the association between preprocedural frailty and long-term all-cause mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from database inception to 15 February 2026. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to pool adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) with their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
Thirteen cohort studies involving 429,827 patients were included in the systematic review. Of these, 8 studies (4,726 patients) reporting comparable adjusted effect estimates were included in the quantitative meta-analysis. Preprocedural frailty was associated with a higher risk of long-term all-cause mortality after TAVR (HR = 1.85, 95% CI 1.51-2.25; I² = 39.4%). The association was generally consistent across subgroup analyses stratified by follow-up duration and frailty assessment methodology. Five studies that were not amenable to quantitative pooling because of non-comparable effect formats or data structures showed a concordant direction of effect, with some studies demonstrating a graded relationship between increasing frailty burden and mortality risk.
Preprocedural frailty is significantly associated with increased long-term all-cause mortality in older adults undergoing TAVR. These findings support the incorporation of frailty assessment into routine preprocedural geriatric risk stratification and multidisciplinary decision-making.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valves among patients with mixed aortic valve disease.
authors: Boren Tan; Qifeng Zhu; Qiong Liu; Wenjing Sheng; Kaida Ren; Yuchao Guo; Xinping Lin; Feiyu Wu; Si Cheng; Chongzhou Zheng; Xianbao Liu
abstract:
Mixed aortic valve disease (MAVD), defined as the coexistence of significant aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Prior studies rarely distinguished bicuspid valve morphology in MAVD populations, and no study has evaluated long-term transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients in this setting. The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.
Between March 2013 and December 2024, 610 MAVD patients undergoing TAVR were included. Patients with severe AS and concomitant presence of moderate or more severe aortic regurgitation were defined as the MAVD. Clinical outcomes, functional status and echocardiography were followed and compared.
A total of 610 patients were included in this study, 220 (36.1%) of whom were BAV morphology. BAV patients were younger (73 vs. 75 years, p < 0.001) and had a lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score (3.47% vs. 4.15%, p < 0.001) compared to TAV patients. The five-year mortality rate was lower in bicuspid than tricuspid patients (10.5% vs. 18.7%, log-rank p = 0.014), while Cox regression analysis did not indicate BAV as an independent predictor of five-year all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47-1.22, p = 0.253). During the one-year follow-up after procedure, BAV patients exhibited a greater increase in AVA and LVEF (p for interaction = 0.012 and 0.011, respectively), and a greater reduction in mean gradient and peak velocity (both p for interaction < 0.001). Meanwhile, similar left ventricular reverse remodelling was found during follow-up (both p for trend < 0.001).
In MAVD patients undergoing TAVR, bicuspid and tricuspid valve morphologies demonstrated comparable long-term clinical outcomes. BAV patients demonstrated greater improvements in left ventricular function and transvalvular hemodynamics, suggesting that bicuspid morphology itself does not confer an adverse long-term prognostic effect in appropriately selected patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.

title: Cardiovascular disease in diabetes mellitus: beyond atherosclerosis and heart failure.
authors: Joanna Y Gong; Spiros Fourlanos; Javed Butler; Peter M Kistler; Christopher M Reid; Dianna J Magliano; Jonathan E Shaw
abstract: The global burden of diabetes mellitus continues to grow, now affecting one in nine adults. In people with diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and considerable focus has been placed on reducing the incidence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure over the past few decades. Due to reductions in the prevalence of some major risk factors, improved control of other risk factors and improved therapeutic agents, mortality attributed to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease has declined. Meanwhile, the decline in mortality attributed to heart failure has stalled. However, beyond atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure, many other cardiovascular diseases are responsible for morbidity and mortality. We provide a comprehensive narrative summary of the association between diabetes mellitus and the most common cardiovascular diseases as reported by the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. The evidence indicates that diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for atrial fibrillation, infective endocarditis, hypertensive heart disease, intracerebral haemorrhage and aortic stenosis. We also discuss the available evidence for the effects of incretin hormone mimetics, such as glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, and of sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors for each of these cardiovascular diseases. This Review underscores the multifaceted link between cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus, highlighting that integrated strategies are required to effectively reduce the global burden of both conditions.

title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve With Preserved Ejection Fraction: One-Year Changes in Ventricular and Atrial Mechanics.
authors: Hakan Yalman; Ahmet Atıl Aygün; Mahmut Kaan Temiz; Damla Raimoglou; Murat Çimci
abstract:
Left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease may precede ejection fraction (EF) decline. We assessed 1-year changes in LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial (LA) strain and myocardial work in BAV with preserved EF.
This retrospective cohort included 82 adults with BAV and sinus rhythm who had preserved LVEF (≥50%) at two echocardiograms 363 ± 15 days apart without interim surgery; 40 age- and sex-matched controls with tricuspid aortic valves were imaged once. Primary outcomes were changes in absolute GLS and LA reservoir strain (LASr); myocardial work, corrected for the transaortic gradient in aortic stenosis, was exploratory. Reader reproducibility was tested on stored images.
At baseline, patients had lower absolute GLS (17.8 ± 2.8% vs. 21.8 ± 1.0%) and LASr (38.5 ± 5.2% vs. 40.8 ± 3.4%) than controls (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004). At 1 year, mean LVEF and LV volumes did not change significantly, whereas absolute GLS decreased by 0.8% points (95% CI 0.5-1.1) and LASr by 2.4 points (1.7-3.0; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Gradient-corrected global work index decreased by 47 mmHg% (27-68). The GLS decrease exceeded the intra-observer minimal detectable change in 22 patients (27%), versus an increase in 4 (5%). The GLS change was not significantly associated with valve lesion type or severity.
In selected patients with BAV who maintained preserved LVEF without valve or aortic surgery, LV GLS and LA reservoir strain decreased slightly over 1 year. Their clinical significance requires validation with longitudinal controls and test-retest data.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Maximilian Autherith; Katharina Singer; Laurenz Hauptmann; Christoph Torrefranca; Charlotte Jantsch; Sophia Koschatko; Eva-Maria Röglsperger; Kseniya Halavina; Gregor Heitzinger; Varius Dannenberg; Raghuram Palaparti; Severin Längle; Stéphane Mahr; Caglayan Demirel; Iuliana Coti; Daniel Zimpfer; Christian Hengstenberg; Christian Nitsche; Philipp E Bartko
abstract:
In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking.
To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes.
DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026.
Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group.
The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points.
Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36).
In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients.

title: Accelerated aortic stenosis progression is associated with greater CT-derived extracellular volume.
authors: André Lobo; José Cavadas; Marta Catarina Almeida; Mariana Brandão; Rafael Teixeira; Carolina Castro; Nuno Dias Ferreira; Pedro Braga; Francisco Sampaio; Ricardo Fontes-Carvalho
journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
abstract: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial changes accompanying faster progression remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between the rate of AS progression and myocardial fibrosis assessed by computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV), and the impact on clinical outcomes. We studied 134 patients with classical high-gradient severe AS who underwent pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation cardiac CT with a delayed dual-energy acquisition for ECV quantification and had at least two echocardiograms ≥ 6 months apart. Progression was defined as the annualized change in peak aortic jet velocity. Rapid progression was defined as an increase > 0.30 m/s/year. Patients were followed for a composite of cardiovascular hospitalization, urgent aortic valve replacement, or death. ECV correlated with progression rate (Spearman ρ = 0.33, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, faster progression remained independently associated with ECV (β = 2.52, p = 0.001). Rapid progressors had higher ECV than slow progressors (31.5% vs. 28.3%, p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 16.2 months, 36 patients (26.9%) reached the composite outcome. Patients with both rapid progression and high ECV had an event rate of 69 versus 11 per 100 patient-years in those without (adjusted HR 6.22, 95% CI 3.13-12.32). Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

title: Emergent Re-Do Open Aortic Valvular Repair and Foreign Body Retrieval During TAVR: A Case Report.
authors: Ryan Dougherty; Thida Ong; Michael Morgan; Eric Chiang; Aariya Srinivasan; Sabry Ayad
abstract: A 73-year-old man presented for a transcatheter aortic valve replacement after prosthetic aortic valve dysfunction. During the case, the transvenous pacer lost capture, causing the new prosthetic valve to embolize to the ascending aorta. This case details the intraoperative management throughout the valve deployment, attempted retrieval, and subsequent emergent redo open aortic valve repair with foreign body removal. Complications and considerations of a redo open chest, vasoplegia, cardiopulmonary bypass, aortic dissection, right ventricular failure, heart block, and prosthetic valve embolization are discussed.

title: Immune-driven remodeling in calcific aortic valve disease: mechanisms and immunotherapeutic opportunities.
authors: Xi Zhang; Yi Si; Ling Liao; Yuxiang Wu
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a prevalent degenerative valvular disorder in the aging population, for which no pharmacological therapy has proven effective in halting or reversing disease progression. Over the past decade, CAVD has been increasingly recognized not as a passive degenerative process of calcium deposition, but as an active, inflammation-driven disease characterized by osteogenic remodeling. This process is initiated and sustained by endothelial injury, lipid retention, immune cell infiltration, and phenotypic transition of valvular interstitial cells. Growing evidence indicates that innate and adaptive immune responses may contribute to disease amplification. Innate immune cells propagate local inflammatory signaling through inflammasome activation, extracellular vesicle communication, protease release, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, while adaptive immune cells further shape disease progression by sustaining cytokine networks that promote fibrosis and osteogenic reprogramming within the valvular microenvironment. Based on these mechanistic insights, this review further discusses emerging translational strategies aimed at targeting key pathogenic processes in CAVD, including modulation of inflammatory signaling, restoration of adaptive immune homeostasis, regulation of extracellular matrix remodeling and antifibrotic pathways, inhibition of VIC osteogenic differentiation, as well as development of patient stratification and local drug delivery approaches. Collectively, these strategies may provide a conceptual framework for earlier, non-surgical interventions for CAVD.

title: Remnant-cholesterol-inflammatory-index as a novel predictor of cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular mortality in elderly patients with severe aortic stenosis.
authors: Annamaria Mazzone; Melania Gaggini; Ilenia Foffa; Serena Del Turco; Fabrizio Minichilli; Sergio Berti; Cristina Vassalle
abstract:
Inflammaging activates a vicious cycle common to the progression of structural cardiovascular alterations, cardiometabolic diseases as well as degenerative aortic stenosis (AoS). The remnant cholesterol inflammatory index (RCII) is a new recently proposed biomarker that combines remnant cholesterol and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, resembling inflammaging. However, the role of RCII in terms of cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular mortality in AoS elderly patients has not been evaluated still now.
to assess the association between RCII and cardiovascular risk factors and mortality in AoS elderly patients.
RCII levels correlated with systemic inflammation biomarkers (closer correlation with interleukin-6), glucose, creatinine, vascular endothelial growth factor and frailty in AoS patients. Inverse correlations were observed with albumin (typically reduced in inflammatory states) and with HDL concentration. The Kaplan-Meier survival estimates showed significantly worse survival in patients with elevated RCII levels (p<0.01) (mean follow-up 19 ± 4 months). In an exploratory multivariable Cox analysis, higher RCII was associated with cardiovascular mortality (HR = 3.5, 95% CI: 1.0-12.0).
RCII is associated with cardiometabolic risk and adverse prognosis in elderly patients with AoS, providing an additional perspective on the prognostic implications of the coexistence of lipid abnormalities and low-grade inflammation in this population. However, the limited number of cardiovascular deaths warrants cautious interpretation of this estimate. Moreover, external validation, standardized thresholds, serial measurements, and comparison with established risk models are needed before RCII clinical implementation.

title: Transapical mitral valve-in-ring implantation: Results of the real-world European Tendyne valve-in-ring registry
authors: Julian Maier; Hendrik Ruge; Markus Krane; Sabine Bleiziffer; Kai Peter Friedrichs; Efstratios I. Charitos; Markus Schönburg; Elmar W Kuhn; Cristina Giannini; Marco De Carlo; Rui Campante Teles; Tiago Nolasco; Martin Andreas; Liliane Zillner; Hermann Blessberger; Thomas Lambert; Ilinca Damian; Michael Grund; Andreas F. Zierer; Clemens Steinwender; Jörg Kellermair
abstract: Abstract Objectives Mitral regurgitation (MR) is commonly treated with ring-based annuloplasty. In case of recurrent MR, re-do operations are often denied due to high risk. Transcatheter valve-in-ring (V-i-R) procedures offer an alternative. This study assessed the feasibility and outcomes of using the transapical, repositionable Tendyne valve for off-label mitral V-i-R procedures, as an alternative to balloon-expandable valves like SAPIEN, which face limitations such as paravalvular leakage and LVOT obstruction. Methods The TEND-RING registry is a retrospective, international study with prospective follow-up, including 16 high-risk patients from eight European centers who underwent Tendyne V-i-R procedures between 2017 and 2024. Procedural, 30-day, and long-term outcomes were analyzed. Results Patients were elderly (median age 79.5), predominantly male (81%), with significant comorbidities (STS Risk of Mortality 5.6%, 4.4–7.2%) and severe MR (3 + /4 +). Procedural success was 100%, with no LVOT obstruction or device embolization. MR was reduced to mild or none in all patients. 30-day mortality was 6.3%. Over a median 11-month follow-up, five deaths occurred (31.3%), three from cardiovascular causes (18.75%). Surviving patients showed sustained MR reduction and improved symptoms (89% in NYHA I/II). Ring size analysis suggested a minimum of 36 mm for rigid/semi-rigid rings, while flexible bands allowed successful implantation in sizes as small as 30 mm. Conclusions Tendyne V-i-R procedures are technically feasible, effective, and safe in selected high-risk patients with recurrent MR. Ring size thresholds identified may guide patient selection and procedural planning in future interventions.

title: Enhancing prognostic evaluation in cardiac amyloidosis: PALS, GLS and functional tests beyond KCCQ
authors: Maria Concetta Pastore; Mariangela Vigna; Elisa Giacomin; Sara Rosi; Federica Marrese; Gian Luca Ragazzoni; Flavio D’Ascenzi; Giulia Elena Mandoli; Luna Cavigli; Matteo Cameli; Marta Focardi
abstract: Background Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) often leads to reduced functional abilities, quality of life, and potential psychological repercussions. Several tests assess functional capacity, with the KCCQ score being the most widely used for heart failure symptoms, but it may overly rely on psychological factors. Left atrial (LA) strain indicates left ventricular (LV) diastolic function and filling pressure but doesn't correlate with KCCQ scores. The relationship between other tests and functional capacity or HRQoL (health-related quality of life) in CA remains unexplored. Objective This observational study aimed to assess the correlation between LA strain and LV global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) with functional tests. Furthermore, we aimed to examine their association with NT-proBNP levels and 6MWT in patients affected by CA, encompassing both AL and ATTR subtypes. Methods We enrolled patients with CA during their follow-up visits. They underwent clinical, echocardiographic, functional capacity and quality-of-life assessments, including the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at baseline and after 3–6 months during follow-up visits, while subsequent clinical follow-up was used to ascertain the composite endpoint. The composite endpoint included all-cause mortality, hospitalization or emergency department visit for heart failure, and urgent cardiovascular visits for worsening heart failure symptoms. Deaths were further classified as cardiovascular or non-cardiovascular according to the predefined cause-of-death classification. Results In total, 67 patients diagnosed with CA (48 ATTRwt and 19 AL, average age 78 years, 21% female) were included. At baseline, patients had an LVEF of 53 ± 7%, a LVGLS of −13 ± 6% and mean PALS of 13 ± 7%. Global PALS demonstrated a positive correlation with DASI score ( p = 0.06) and 6MWT ( p = 0.004), and showed an inverse correlation with MLHFQ score ( p = 0.005) and NT-proBNP ( p = 0.003) while it was not correlated with KCCQ ( p = 0.21). GLS demonstrated a positive correlation with NT-proBNP ( p = 0.001), Minnesota score ( p = 0.01), DASI score ( p = 0.017). In contrast, the KCCQ did not correlate with NT-proBNP, PALS, 6MWT, or GLS. 42 patients (62.7%) experienced the composite endpoint. GLS was lower in the event group, PALS was lower, interventricular septal thickness (IVS) was larger, NT-proBNP was greater, and LAVi was higher. Our study showed that LVGLS, PALS, and apical sparing (RELAPS) were associated with the composite clinical endpoint, with LVGLS showing the numerically highest AUC among the evaluated parameters (AUC 0.704 (95% CI: 0.595–0.813) for LVGLS, 0.663 (95% CI: 0.549–0.777) for PALS, and 0.660 (95% CI: 0.545–0.775) for RELAPS). Conclusions LVGLS showed significant associations with functional status and quality-of-life measures and had the numerically highest AUC for the composite clinical endpoint among the evaluated parameters.

title: Association of left atrial strain and stiffness index with ascending aortic dilatation in patients with bicuspid aortic valve
authors: Huan Liu; Kunxuan Liu; Xueting Guo; Caiyun Zhang; Kuican Liu; wenrong Shi; Lei Huang; Wenjuan Qin; Dong Shanshan
abstract: Background Left atrial stiffness index (LASI) is an emerging echocardiographic index that reflects left atrial–left ventricular functional coupling and diastolic dysfunction. However, the relationships of left atrial strain parameters and LASI with ascending aortic dilatation (AAD) in patients with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the associations of left atrial strain parameters and LASI with the presence of AAD and to evaluate their ability to discriminate between BAV patients with and without AAD. Methods and results This retrospective study included 86 patients with BAV and 40 healthy controls. Left atrial reservoir strain (LASr), conduit strain (LAScd), and contraction strain (LASct) were measured, and LASI was calculated. Based on the aortic size index (ASI), patients with BAV were classified into a nondilated group (ASI ≤ 2.1 cm/m 2 ) and a dilated group (ASI > 2.1 cm/m 2 ). In ROC curve analyses, LASr, E/e′ (the ratio of early transmitral flow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity), and LASI demonstrated discriminatory ability for the presence of AAD in patients with BAV, with AUCs of 0.792, 0.783, and 0.871, respectively. The corresponding data-derived optimal cutoff values were 23.44%, 8.17, and 0.30. Multivariable binary logistic regression analysis showed that LASr < 23.44%, E/e′ > 8.17, and LASI > 0.30 were independently associated with the presence of AAD in patients with BAV. When LASI was added to the baseline model comprising E/e′ and LASr, the likelihood-ratio χ 2 increased from 41.88 to 45.84 ( Δχ 2 = 3.96, P = 0.047), with a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.571 (95% CI, 0.193–0.950; P = 0.003). Conclusions LASI was associated with the presence of AAD in patients with BAV and provided incremental discriminatory information within the study sample. As a simple echocardiographic index integrating an estimate of left ventricular filling pressure with left atrial reservoir function, LASI may provide complementary information on left atrial–left ventricular functional alterations in BAV patients with AAD.

title: Beyond Structured Vitals: Semantic-Temporal Alignment for Full-Record ICU Risk Forecasting
authors: Zhichong Zheng; Xiaohang Nie; Xueqi Wang; Yuanjin Zhao; Haitao Zhang; Yichao Tang
journal: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
abstract: Traditional Electronic Health Record (EHR) datasets heavily favor structured data, often missing the nuanced progression of patients in intensive care. To address this gap, we introduce FRICU, a newly constructed dataset integrating structured vitals with full-record clinical narratives across complete admission trajectories using expert-verified, event-level annotations. Recognizing that the pathological impact of historical events depends on their semantic content rather than mere chronological proximity, we propose Semantic-Temporal Alignment (SeTA), a semantic-guided temporal attention mechanism that dynamically calibrates temporal receptive fields for query-specific evidence retrieval. For supervision, expert-verified risk labels are transformed into continuous trajectories via bidirectional Gaussian decay, providing smooth event-level supervision for gradual risk evolution. On FRICU, SeTA achieves a Sample AUPRC of 0.428, improving over TALE-EHR by 21.2%. On MIMIC-IV, SeTA achieves the best AUPRC on IMV and mortality prediction and remains competitive on sepsis prediction, demonstrating generalization beyond text-intensive full-record trajectories. To facilitate reproducibility, our code is available at https://github.com/violetesk/SeTA-FRICU.

title: Myxoedema coma with complete atrioventricular block: a case report
authors: Ahmet Berk Duman; Hayriye Gökalp; Tarık Erçetin; Selçuk Beniz; Denizhan Karaçimen
journal: Exploration of Endocrine and Metabolic Diseases
abstract: Advanced atrioventricular (AV) block can accompany severe hypothyroidism, but thyroid dysfunction does not by itself establish reversibility. A 75-year-old man presented approximately 30 minutes after the onset of dizziness and general deterioration. At the initial documented assessment, temperature was 36.6°C, Glasgow Coma Scale score was 15, oxygen saturation was 98% on room air, and blood pressure was 100/60 mmHg while receiving norepinephrine at 0.05 µg/kg/min. The admission electrocardiogram (ECG) showed complete AV block with an atrial rate of approximately 41–42 beats/min and a markedly slow, wide-complex ventricular escape at approximately 13–14 beats/min. Temporary transvenous pacing increased ventricular rate to approximately 80 beats/min, and coronary angiography showed a dominant right coronary artery, non-obstructive plaques, no culprit lesion, and TIMI 3 flow in all major epicardial vessels. Despite effective rate correction, progressive haemodynamic, respiratory and renal deterioration could no longer be explained by the AV block alone, prompting evaluation for an alternative systemic cause. As respiratory failure progressed, SpO2 fell into the 30% range. At controlled endotracheal intubation, blood pressure was 90/60 mmHg during norepinephrine infusion at 0.2 µg/kg/min, while the temporary pacemaker continued to provide ventricular pacing. Cardiac arrest occurred shortly afterwards, with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 40 minutes of cardiopulmonary resuscitation. After resuscitation, the previously requested thyroid-function results became available and demonstrated severe primary hypothyroidism (TSH 106 mIU/L, fT3 1.18 pg/mL, fT4 0.38 ng/dL); further history revealed approximately one month of levothyroxine non-adherence. The evolving multisystem syndrome yielded a score of 120 under the 2026 joint-consensus adaptation of the Popoveniuc system, highly suggestive of myxoedema coma. Intravenous hydrocortisone and levothyroxine were initiated. Refractory shock and multiorgan failure persisted, and the patient died on day 3. This case highlights that restoring ventricular rate may not correct a concurrent systemic endocrine crisis and that thyroid dysfunction alone does not prove AV-block reversibility.

title: Myeloid–fibroblast–cardiomyocyte crosstalk in atrial fibrillation: hypertension and evidence across disease models
authors: Shengbo Bi; Yuzhang Sun; Xinfu Zou; Xiaofeng Ruan; Jin Zhu
abstract: Hypertension is a major antecedent of atrial fibrillation, but pressure load alone does not explain the development of an arrhythmogenic atrial substrate. Wall stress and neurohumoral activation can recruit circulating myeloid cells, alter macrophage states, activate fibroblasts, and disrupt cardiomyocyte inflammatory signaling and calcium handling. This review examines evidence from hypertensive animals, mixed-risk-factor models, human atrial tissue, and non-hypertensive models, separating findings demonstrated in each setting from their proposed relevance to hypertension. Macrophage osteopontin promotes fibroblast matrix programs in mixed-risk-factor models. Fibroblast-restricted NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation promotes fibrosis and conduction abnormalities in a non-hypertensive model. Separate experiments link cardiomyocyte NLRP3 or N-terminal gasdermin D signaling to inflammatory output and arrhythmogenic remodeling. These mechanisms may converge, but neither a serial osteopontin–fibroblast NLRP3 pathway nor a complete three-cell causal circuit has been established in hypertension. Blood-pressure-matched experiments, spatially resolved human atrial studies, and interventions that distinguish recruited pathological states from resident reparative macrophages are needed to test these links. Such studies may identify the disease stages and cell states in which immune modulation can complement control of hemodynamic stress.

title: ACUTE HYPOXEMIC RESPIRATORY FAILURE WITH SEVERE HYPERLACTATEMIA AND MIXED ACID–BASE DISORDER IN A PATIENT WITH PREVIOUS MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION: A CASE REPORT
authors: Budi Anugrah; Hersa Donantya Daneswara
journal: The International Journal of Medical Science and Health Research
abstract: Introduction: Acute heart failure (AHF) presenting as acute pulmonary edema is a leading cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF). Elevated lactate identifies organ injury and a worse prognosis in AHF even without overt hypoperfusion, and lactate combined with acidemia strongly modifies mortality in cardiogenic shock; when severe hyperlactatemia coexists with a primary respiratory alkalosis, a near-normal pH may conceal the true metabolic severity.1–3 Case illustration: A 48-year-old man with a previous ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and a prior episode of AHF presented with dyspnea since the previous night, respiratory rate 41 breaths/min, SpO2 78% on room air (87% on a non-rebreathing mask), blood pressure 148/103 mmHg, heart rate 120 beats/min, warm extremities and bilateral crackles with wheezing. Arterial blood gas (reported FiO2 0.81) showed pH 7.35, PaCO2 21 mmHg, PaO2 52 mmHg, HCO3− 11.8 mmol/L, base excess −14 mmol/L and lactate 11.20 mmol/L; PaCO2 below the Winter's range (23.7–27.7 mmHg) indicated a concurrent primary respiratory alkalosis. High-sensitivity troponin I was 65.2 pg/mL (≈1.7 × upper reference limit), creatinine 1.84 mg/dL, potassium 2.8 mmol/L and glucose 300 mg/dL. Despite nitroglycerin, furosemide and mask oxygen he required intubation, after which high respiratory drive (total rate 43 breaths/min; tidal volume ≈10.6 mL/kg predicted body weight), severe hypoxemia (SpO2 93% on FiO2 0.85) and a fall in blood pressure to 101/55 mmHg were documented.4–6 Discussion: The ≈13% reduction in arterial oxygen content could not by itself explain a lactate of 11.2 mmol/L, implying superimposed normotensive low-output hypoperfusion, catecholamine-driven aerobic glycolysis—mirrored by hypokalemia and hyperglycemia—alkalosis-enhanced glycolysis, increased work of breathing and reduced clearance. The near-normal pH concealed a profound base deficit, a metabolic–hemodynamic discordance poorly captured by blood pressure-based staging, while vigorous post-intubation effort carried a risk of patient self-inflicted lung injury.7–10 Conclusion: In AHF complicated by AHRF, severe hyperlactatemia with a mixed acid–base disorder is a high-risk phenotype even when blood pressure is preserved. Systematic acid–base analysis, serial lactate, early echocardiography and lung ultrasound, timely evaluation for acute coronary syndrome, potassium repletion before or with insulin and diuretics, and lung-protective ventilation that controls respiratory drive are essential.11,12

title: Evaluation of risk factors for tricuspid regurgitation prior to cardiac pacemaker
authors: Shuangling Wang; Qiuzhe Guo; Li Li; Guochun Li; Ying Zhou; Yunfei Zhou; Guodong Niu; Yulong Guo
abstract: Objective To identify factors associated with preprocedural tricuspid regurgitation (TR) in patients with bradyarrhythmia undergoing cardiac pacemaker implantation and to evaluate the impact of preprocedural TR severity on postprocedural TR evolution and clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective study included 767 patients with bradyarrhythmia who underwent permanent pacemaker implantation at Fuwai Yunnan Cardiovascular Hospital between January 2020 and October 2024. Patients were stratified into four groups according to preprocedural TR severity: none, mild, moderate, and severe. Clinical data, laboratory parameters, and echocardiographic parameters were collected. Univariate analysis was used to compare differences among groups, and ordinal logistic regression was used to identify independent factors associated with preprocedural TR. Among the 501 patients with follow-up of at least 2 months, binary logistic regression was used to evaluate the impact of preprocedural TR on postprocedural outcomes. Results Multivariable analysis showed that female sex (OR = 1.573), heart failure (OR = 1.837), persistent atrial fibrillation (OR = 4.958), and pulmonary hypertension (OR = 6.586) were independent risk factors for greater preprocedural TR severity, whereas higher BMI (OR = 0.920) was an independent protective factor (all P < 0.05). At a median follow-up of 16 months after pacemaker implantation, greater preprocedural TR severity was associated with more frequent postprocedural rehospitalizations ( P = 0.007) and a higher risk of cardiac function deterioration ( P < 0.001). Compared with patients without preprocedural TR, those with moderate or severe preprocedural TR had a significantly lower risk of postprocedural TR worsening and a higher rate of TR improvement, with this benefit being more pronounced in younger patients. Conclusions In patients with bradyarrhythmia undergoing cardiac pacing, preprocedural TR severity is influenced by multiple factors, including sex, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and pulmonary hypertension. Greater preprocedural TR severity is associated with worse postprocedural cardiac functional outcomes. Among patients with pre-existing moderate-to-severe TR, a substantial proportion show improvement in TR after pacemaker implantation, and younger patients are more likely to benefit from such improvement. Cardiac pacing does not exert exclusively detrimental effects on TR.

title: Cardiac MRI-derived extracellular volume fraction is associated with failed left ventricular reverse remodeling after aortic valve replacement in severe aortic regurgitation With a giant left ventricle
authors: Hao Niu; Yangbo Yan; Xiangfeng Gong; Xiao Xiao; Changping Gan; ZhengHua Xiao
abstract: Severe chronic aortic regurgitation (AR) with a markedly dilated left ventricle (LV) (‘giant left ventricle’; LV end-diastolic diameter, LVEDD ≥65 mm) carries a high risk of incomplete LV reverse remodeling after aortic valve replacement (AVR), yet reliable preoperative stratification tools remain limited. This retrospective cohort study aimed to evaluate whether preoperative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) is associated with 6-month LV reverse remodeling in this high-risk population. We enrolled 46 consecutive patients with severe AR and LVEDD ≥65 mm receiving contrast-enhanced CMR and elective AVR. The primary analysis assessed the association between preoperative ECV and the continuous relative change in LVEDD at 6 months; a binary definition (≥20% LVEDD reduction) was used as a secondary, clinically oriented outcome. Absence of significant LV reverse remodeling (<20% reduction) was observed in 47.8% (22/46) of patients. In linear regression analysis, higher preoperative ECV was significantly associated with a smaller LVEDD reduction ( β = −0.924 per 1% absolute increase in ECV, 95% CI −1.528 to −0.320, P = 0.004). In multivariable logistic regression restricted to the preoperative variables significant on univariable analysis (ECV and LVEDD), ECV remained associated with failed reverse remodeling (adjusted OR = 1.281 per 1% absolute increase in ECV, 95% CI 1.001–1.640, P = 0.049), although the association attenuated after further adjustment for age (OR 1.227, 95% CI 0.950–1.585, P = 0.117); with an exploratory cutoff of 34.1% (AUC=0.74, 95%CI 0.59–0.89). Patients with ECV >34.1% exhibited impaired postoperative LV systolic function and prolonged hospital stay. These exploratory findings suggest that preoperative CMR-ECV may help identify severe AR patients at risk of incomplete LV reverse remodeling after AVR, and warrant prospective validation.

title: Early postoperative endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) as a novel biomarker for delirium and mortality after cardiac valve replacement surgery: a retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database
authors: Pan Li; Ran Duan; Qiang Sun; Longlu Cao; Jianli Li
abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) following cardiac valve replacement surgery is a serious complication that impacts patient prognosis. However, effective early postoperative risk stratification tools integrating key pathophysiological mechanisms are currently lacking. Endothelial dysfunction and systemic inflammation are core mechanisms underlying POD, and the endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX), as a novel composite biomarker reflecting endothelial injury and inflammatory stress, has not yet been clearly established as a predictive tool in cardiac surgery. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of individuals undergoing cardiac valve replacement surgery based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Individuals were divided into quartile groups according to their early postoperative EASIX levels. The primary outcome was POD, and the secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were adopted to appraise the association between EASIX and the outcomes, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were employed to ascertain the dose-response relationship. Furthermore, a random forest prediction model incorporating EASIX was constructed for POD within 28 days and internally validated using 10-fold cross-validation. Totally 1,543 individuals were finally included, with an incidence rate of POD of 36.2% and an in-hospital mortality rate of 4.3%. Cox regression analysis showed that a higher early postoperative EASIX level was an independent risk determinant for POD (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) = 1.185, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.072–1.309; P < 0.001) and in-hospital mortality (adjusted HR = 1.521, 95% CI: 1.190–1.943; P < 0.001). The trend test revealed a significant increase in the risk of all outcomes across increasing EASIX quartiles (all P for trend < 0.05). RCS analysis demonstrated an approximately linear positive correlation between EASIX and risk. The random forest model showed moderate discrimination in 10-fold cross-validation (area under the curve (AUC) = 63.8%). In conclusion, early postoperative EASIX was substantially linked to POD and in-hospital mortality after cardiac valve replacement surgery. Being easily obtainable from routine tests, it holds potential for clinical translation and provides a novel and practical tool for early postoperative identification of high-risk patients.

title: Pathophysiological Concepts in Cardiovascular Medicine: Update 2026
authors: Asad Ali Ahmed Cheema; Ayesha Ahmed Cheema; Eshal Muhammad; Ali Akbar Mithani
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet classification still relies largely on anatomy, hemodynamics, and function, which can group patients with different underlying disease biology. Human studies across cardiovascular conditions now identify vascular, myocardial, metabolic, renal, hematologic, and peripheral processes that modify disease expression beyond conventional labels. Atherogenic particle burden, lipoprotein(a), clonal hematopoiesis, myocardial energetic and genetic abnormalities, chamber remodeling, dysfunctional adiposity, iron deficiency, skeletal muscle dysfunction, and cancer-associated cardiac wasting illustrate how similar phenotypes can arise from different substrates. These observations are supported to varying degrees by genetic, longitudinal, imaging, physiological, tissue, and interventional evidence, and their relative importance differs across patients and disease stages. Association with disease severity or outcome should therefore not be interpreted automatically as causal or therapeutically modifiable. Longitudinal phenotyping can clarify temporal relationships, while mechanistic studies should establish target engagement and the expected biological or physiological response. Clinical outcome trials must then determine whether modifying a candidate pathway improves patient-relevant outcomes. Mechanistically informed phenotyping may complement established cardiovascular classification by refining patient selection, distinguishing clinically meaningful substrates from associated signals, and supporting mechanism-directed therapeutic development where the evidence is sufficiently robust, rather than replacing established clinical disease labels.

title: Ultrasound-based assessment of cardiac and hepatic dysfunction: current status and future directions
authors: Yin-Xia Li; Lei Chen; Peng Chen; Yi-Sheng Wang; Rui Shen
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a systemic syndrome in which venous congestion and impaired perfusion can produce clinically important hepatic dysfunction. The term cardiohepatic syndrome (CHS) describes this bidirectional interaction, but cardiac and hepatic abnormalities are still often evaluated in parallel rather than as a connected hemodynamic process. Ultrasound is uniquely suited to an integrated assessment because it can characterize cardiac structure and function, systemic venous congestion, hepatic hemodynamics, tissue stiffness, and treatment-related change at the bedside. Conventional transthoracic echocardiography remains the foundation of evaluation, while three-dimensional echocardiography and speckle-tracking techniques improve quantification of right ventricular, atrial, and subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Abdominal Doppler ultrasound, venous congestion scoring, and liver elastography add complementary information, although liver stiffness must be interpreted cautiously because congestion, inflammation, cholestasis, and fibrosis can produce overlapping signals. Artificial intelligence may improve acquisition, measurement reproducibility, and multimodal data integration, but external validation and transparent reporting remain essential. This review summarizes contemporary evidence and proposes a practical, sequential pathway that combines echocardiography, venous Doppler findings, liver stiffness, laboratory biomarkers, and dynamic reassessment after decongestion. The central clinical principle is that CHS should be evaluated as a time-varying cardiohepatic phenotype rather than diagnosed from a single cardiac, hepatic, or biochemical measurement. Integrated ultrasound assessment of cardiohepatic syndrome. Heart failure produces a continuum from myocardial dysfunction and elevated filling pressures to systemic venous congestion, hepatic sinusoidal stress, and potentially fibrosis. A combined protocol uses echocardiography to define the cardiac substrate, venous Doppler ultrasound to quantify pressure transmission, and liver elastography plus biomarkers to characterize hepatic injury. Dynamic reassessment after decongestion helps distinguish reversible congestion from persistent structural liver disease and supports risk-adapted management.

title: Challenges and innovations in cardiac AAV gene delivery as a platform for cardiac regeneration
authors: Gabriella Kabboul; Alejandro Izurieta Muñoz; Muath M. Bishawi; Christopher B. Doering; Rebecca D. Levit
abstract: Gene therapies are at the forefront of potential treatments for cardiovascular diseases, but clinical translation remains limited by poor myocardial access and retention, systemic distribution, and immune-mediated toxicities. Heavily underexplored, the route of administration dictates efficacy and safety, ultimately influencing therapeutic outcomes. This review addresses the role of delivery in overcoming these challenges in cardiac adeno-associated viral therapies. Emphasis is placed on biomaterial-based delivery approaches to improve therapeutic outcomes.

title: Physiological markers of low-altitude exercise load for predicting acute mountain sickness: development of an interpretable machine learning model and research web calculator
authors: Fengbo Miao; Yi Yuan; Shuai Wang; Chengli Tao; Yupeng Liu; Qi Mao; Hualin Zhang; Ning Li; Renzheng Chen; Jianfu Sui
abstract: Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses a significant threat to individuals ascending to high-altitude regions, yet early identification of susceptible populations remains challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for estimating AMS risk from exercise-induced physiological responses measured at low altitude. A total of 171 healthy participants were included, with 111 participants (51 AMS events) comprising the development cohort and 60 participants (27 AMS events) forming an external validation cohort. Model development was repeated within a nested cross-validation framework, including LASSO feature selection and algorithm selection within the resampling process. The final locked five-feature model included changes in post-exercise pulse oxygen saturation (ΔSpO 2 ) and cardiac output (ΔCO), sex, smoking history, and drinking history, and combined logistic regression, support vector machine, and random forest by equal-weight soft voting. In the development cohort, pooled outer-fold predictions yielded an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI, 0.791–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.842 (95% CI, 0.748–0.932), and a Brier score of 0.148. The calibration intercept was −0.033 (95% CI, −0.504 to 0.527), the calibration slope was 0.931 (95% CI, 0.664–1.351) and the positive net benefit range was 0.078–0.840. In the external validation cohort, the locked model yielded an AUC of 0.834 (95% CI, 0.723–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.867 (95% CI, 0.758–0.946), and a Brier score of 0.152; the calibration intercept was −0.103 (95% CI, −0.834 to 0.531), the calibration slope was 1.013 (95% CI, 0.655–1.666) and a positive net benefit range of 0.200–0.953. Post-hoc SHAP analysis identified ΔSpO 2 and ΔCO as the two most influential predictors. These findings support an association between low-altitude exercise responses and subsequent AMS. However, the prediction model requires further development and validation in substantially larger cohorts before clinical deployment.

title: Mechanosensing channels PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 regulate mitral valve serotonin-mediated homeostasis and pathophysiology
authors: Emily Hall
abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) pathophysiology involves increased serotonin (5-HT) receptor (HTR) expression and signalling, together with reduced 5-HT transporter (SLC6A4) expression in mitral valve interstitial cells (MVIC). The mechanosensitive calcium channels, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2, regulate cellular responses to a variety of mechanical conditions; however, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 have not been studied in MR. We investigated the hypothesis that PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 mediate, through 5-HT mechanisms, both homeostasis in normal mitral valves (nMV) and in the pathophysiology of MR.

title: Systemic Laboratory Alterations Associated With Heart Failure in Severe Mitral Regurgitation: A Retrospective Observational Study
authors: Emilia Sorina Fiat; Nastaca Alina Palade; Crina Cristina Solomon; Razvan Constantin Vonica; Bogdan Ioan Vintilă; Maria Totan; Anca Maria Arseniu; Claudiu Morgovan; Anca Butucă; Adina Frum; Carmen Maximiliana Dobrea; Diter Atasie; Felicia Gabriela Gligor
abstract: Background: The systemic laboratory abnormalities accompanying documented heart failure in patients hospitalized with severe mitral regurgitation (MR) have not been fully characterized across multiple biological domains within the same cohort.Methodology: In this retrospective, single-center, cross-sectional study, 107 adults with echocardiographically documented severe MR were compared according to the presence (n = 49) or absence (n = 58) of a heart failure diagnosis at discharge.Inflammatory, hematological, renal, electrolyte, hepatic, and coagulation measures were evaluated using multiplicity-adjusted comparisons and age-and sexadjusted domain-specific logistic regression.A post hoc model integrating age, sex, C-reactive protein, anemia, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73m² was explored using sensitivity analyses and fixed-model bootstrap validation.Results: Multiple laboratory domains differed by heart failure status.In the post hoc integrated model, eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m² showed the most consistent association with concomitant heart failure (odds ratio, 5.56; 95% confidence interval, 1.94-15.94;P = 0.001); C-reactive protein and anemia were not statistically significant after mutual adjustment.The apparent and optimism-corrected areas under the curve were 0.809 and 0.780, respectively; corresponding Brier scores were 0.175 and 0.196.Conclusions: Among hospitalized patients with severe MR, documented concomitant heart failure was accompanied by abnormalities across several laboratory domains, with reduced renal function showing the most consistent association in exploratory multivariable analyses.The retrospective design, dischargediagnosis-based heart failure classification, incomplete echocardiographic characterization, and limited sample size preclude causal or predictive interpretations.

title: May-Thurner Syndrome Presenting as Submassive Pulmonary Embolism in a Young Male: A Case Report
authors: Anita Ho; Colleen Chen; Suchith B Suresh; Omar Adeeb; Helen Stutz
abstract: May-Thurner syndrome (MTS) is an anatomic variant in which the right common iliac artery compresses the left common iliac vein, predisposing to left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT).While MTS predominantly affects young women, we present a case of a 24-year-old African American male with a family history suggestive of hereditary hypercoagulability who developed a massive bilateral pulmonary embolism (PE) with right heart strain and extensive left lower extremity DVT, revealing underlying MTS as the anatomic substrate for his thrombotic event.Management included systemic anticoagulation, mechanical pulmonary thrombectomy, and percutaneous lower extremity thrombectomy, with plans for outpatient hypercoagulability evaluation.

title: Echocardiographic phenotypes of opioid-induced cardiotoxicity: a narrative review
authors: Krzysztof Żerdziński; Julita Janiec; Alexander Suchodolski; Mariola Szulik
abstract: Opioid cardiotoxicity is an increasing clinical concern, yet its echocardiographic manifestations are heterogeneous and poorly characterized. This narrative review synthesizes available evidence, maps the principal echocardiographic phenotypes of opioid-related cardiac injury, and identifies major knowledge gaps. A structured PubMed search (January 2014-December 2024) combined opioid and echocardiographic terms without language restriction. Human and animal studies of any design assessing cardiac structure or function by echocardiography after acute or chronic opioid exposure were eligible. Of 209 records, 41 were included and grouped by dominant phenotype. No formal protocol (e.g., PRISMA) or risk-of-bias appraisal was applied. Five distinct-and often conflicting-phenotypes emerged: (1) severe, potentially reversible global left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF as low as 20%), sometimes progressing to cardiogenic shock yet normalising within 48-72 h; (2) Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, classic after withdrawal and predominantly reverse after intoxication; (3) right ventricular dysfunction with pulmonary hypertension, usually secondary to hypoxia or left-sided failure but occasionally isolated; (4) consistent cardioprotection in animal ischaemia-reperfusion models, unsupported by any prospective human echocardiographic study; and (5) a mechanically normal profile despite QTc exceeding 610 ms and torsades de pointes. Phenotypes 1-3 rest largely on case reports, and many studies are confounded by co-administered cocaine, benzodiazepines or α2-adrenoceptor agonists. Opioid cardiac effects are context-dependent, and mechanical toxicity diverges from electrical toxicity: a normal echocardiogram does not exclude lethal arrhythmia, so echocardiography and serial QTc assessment are complementary rather than interchangeable. Prospective studies with advanced imaging are needed to establish phenotype frequency and determinants.

title: Differential hypoxaemia before aortic cross-clamping during minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: a case report
authors: Kübra Gözaçık Karakoç; Şahin Kapan; Veli Tackin; Nevzat Erdil
abstract: Differential hypoxaemia, also known as Harlequin syndrome or North–South syndrome, occurs during peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass when poorly oxygenated blood ejected by the native heart competes with retrograde oxygenated blood delivered from a femoral arterial cannula, so that the aortic arch vessels and the cerebral circulation may be perfused with deoxygenated blood. It is well described in venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation but is a less familiar complication of minimally invasive cardiac surgery. We report its occurrence before aortic cross-clamping during minimally invasive mitral valve surgery, whilst native ejection was presumed to persist and pulmonary ventilation had been suspended for surgical exposure. A 38-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease and severe mitral regurgitation (left ventricular ejection fraction 60%) underwent minimally invasive mitral valve surgery through a right anterior minithoracotomy with peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass established by femoral cannulation. Invasive arterial pressure was monitored from the right radial artery. Before aortic cross-clamping, whilst native ejection was presumed to persist, the blood visible in the aortic root vent line of the vented antegrade cardioplegia cannula appeared darker and the right-hand oxygen saturation fell to approximately 50%; arterial blood gas analysis showed a partial pressure of oxygen of 226 mmHg in the oxygenator outflow but only 23 mmHg in the right radial artery, confirming differential hypoxaemia. Two-lung ventilation was resumed, and the right-hand oxygen saturation recovered promptly. A 31-mm mechanical prosthesis was implanted and the patent foramen ovale was closed through the same incision. The patient was extubated 4 h postoperatively without clinically apparent neurological deficit and was discharged on postoperative day 5, remaining in New York Heart Association class I at five months. Differential hypoxaemia can complicate minimally invasive mitral valve surgery when antegrade native output persists. Right radial arterial monitoring provides a sentinel indicator of oxygenation in the brachiocephalic territory and allowed early recognition in this patient. Early restoration of pulmonary gas exchange may limit severe upper-body hypoxaemic exposure and potentially reduce neurological risk.
